rationale: I read the complete held EO 9762 (11 FR 8073, signed July 25, 1946): it transfers the Office of Economic Stabilization (EOs 9250 and 9699), with its functions, records, property, personnel and funds, to the Office of War Mobilization and Reconversion; transfers the Economic Stabilization Director's functions to the Director of War Mobilization and Reconversion; transfers the Economic Stabilization Board to OWMR to advise the Director; keeps prior OES regulations in effect; and amends conflicting prior orders. It has no own term. No held instrument revokes EO 9762 by name; its end rests on the displacement of every arrangement it made. I read the held full text of EO 9809 (11 FR 14281, signed December 12, 1946, Providing for the Disposition of Certain War Agencies): para. 1 consolidates OWMR and OES (with OPA and CPA) into one agency, the Office of Temporary Controls; para. 2 vests the functions of the Director of War Mobilization and Reconversion and of the Economic Stabilization Director in the Temporary Controls Administrator; para. 3(b) provides 'The Economic Stabilization Board (transferred to the Office of War Mobilization and Reconversion by Executive Order No. 9762 of July 25, 1946) and its functions are terminated'; para. 12 amends conflicting prior orders. After EO 9809 nothing EO 9762 placed in OWMR remains there: OES and OWMR are merged into OTC, the Director's role passes to the Administrator, and the Board is abolished. I read the held EO 9841 (12 FR 2645, signed April 23, 1947, Termination of the Office of Temporary Controls): sec. 204 revokes 'Executive Order No. 9705 of March 15, 1946 (as modified by Executive Orders Nos. 9762 and 9809)', removing EO 9762's amendment of EO 9705, and sec. 303 (effective June 1, 1947) provides that the Office of Temporary Controls is terminated. EO 9762's own savings sentence continues OES regulations, not the order. D6 self-check: EO 9801 (November 9, 1946), the actor in the 1989 snapshot row, terminates wage and salary controls under the Stabilization Act and does not name EO 9762; it narrows the OES functions but is not the end. A search of the held full-run texts for '9762' finds EO 9809, EO 9841 and page-number hits in the unrelated EO 9774 and EO 9775 contents columns; no held later instrument names or restores EO 9762. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 9809, December 12, 1946' is read as this displacement, since EO 9809 has no express revocation verb for EO 9762. The ACT@75065fec record (APP transcription) is the para. 3(b) slice, which the official FR text matches. Both history observations (API catalog record and S1989 row) were reviewed. Provisional NO hypothesis; the first end (December 12, 1946 by displacement, or June 1, 1947 when OTC ended) is an open point, not adjudicated.
